sonnet.problem: The card says David was waiting in the pit ('David wasn't waiting somewhere nice. He was down in the pit...'). Verse 1 says he waited, and verse 2 says the LORD lifted him from the pit. The text never says he waited in the pit, so the card adds how the two connect.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The Hebrews 10 fulfillment takes up most of the card, a full sentence rather than a few words. The card's verses field is also 'Psalm 40:6-8', but the Psalm part of the card tells only the second half of verse 8 ('Your law is within my heart').
sonnet.rule: An outside passage, like a New Testament fulfillment, only rides along in a few words on a card that tells this passage. It never gets a card of its own

sonnet.problem: The card quotes the heavy line about evils and sins more than the hairs of his head and a failed heart, then jokes about counting hairs in the mustache. That is a joke on a card that tells serious sin and despair, where care should be shown instead.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke. He can show care instead, marked as his own ("I think this one hurts").

sonnet.problem: The card calls those who say 'Aha, aha!' 'mockers'. The text only says 'those who say to me, "Aha, aha!"' and never names them mockers or gives their intent.
sonnet.rule: Call things what the text calls them.
